subject: Tenant deletion SLA + region preference — productization sync
content:
From: Lucy Parker <lucy.parker@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Retention + deletion SLA requirements for Acme pilot

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move forward with the pilot, legal requested confirmation that we can meet a 30-day deletion SLA for tenant data and that data copies will be restricted to US regions only (no cross-border replication). They also asked for an auditable deletion proof (deletion event + log entries) and a mechanism to mark specific datasets as exempt for longer retention if required by their audit team.

Can you share whether Redwood has a roadmap to expose per-tenant retention windows and a per-tenant region preference setting (i.e., pin tenant to US-only storage)? If not, can you outline interim controls we can use (e.g., configurable lifecycle policies, manual processes) and an ETA if this is planned?

I've attached our retention matrix and a short list of legal questions for reference.

Thanks,
Lucy
Lucy Parker
Head of Cloud Ops — Acme Financial Services
attachments: acme-retention-requirements.pdf, deletion-sla-matrix.xlsx

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention + deletion SLA requirements for Acme pilot

Hi Lucy — looping in product and security so we can give a consolidated answer. Short answer: we do not yet have a per-tenant region pinning UI, but we can support region-scoped storage and retention enforcement via configuration at the customer deployment layer. We also support deletion events and an audit log stream that records object-level delete operations (we'll need to map that to your legal team's requirements).

Priya/Karthik/Mina — please see Lucy's attached matrix and the three asks: (1) 30-day deletion SLA with auditable proof, (2) US-only storage/pinning, (3) dataset-level exemptions. Can you outline a productization path (API + UI) and any constraints that might affect ETA? If we need a short-term workaround for the pilot, propose one we can commit to for 1–3 months.

Rishi

On Fri, 25 Jun 2027 at 10:40 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example.com> wrote:

> Thanks for the ping, Rishi — and hi Lucy. I pulled together a proposal below for how we can productize tenant-level retention and region preference without a major re-architecture. High-level: add a policy layer (tenantRetentionPolicy) that is authoritative for serving and storage routing, and expose it via a REST API + Console UI.
>
> Proposed surface and timeline (MVP):
> - API: /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy — fields: retention_days, region_preference (enum: us, eu, apac, multi), exemption_tags (list), enforce_immediate_deletion (bool)
> - Console: Tenant settings page with toggle + TTL selector + region dropdown + exemption tag editor (mockup attached)
> - Enforcement: control-plane policy propagated to storage layer and serving runtime; deletion requests produce a signed deletion event + audit log entry in our audit stream (retained per contract)
> - Rollout: canary with 5 pilot tenants -> general availability in 10 weeks (engineering dependent)
>
> Short-term workarounds for the pilot:
> - Per-tenant lifecycle policy: we can set a storage lifecycle rule that hard-deletes objects after X days at the storage tier (best-effort for cross-region copies)
> - Manual region restriction: provision a US-only storage bucket for Acme and bind the tenant to that bucket (requires ops intervention; no console toggle)
> - Audit deliverable: export of deletion events + signed note from operations for the pilot window
>
> Ask from engineering/security to finalize estimates:
> 1) Can the serving runtime honor policy changes to immediately evict KV caches and block reads from deleted objects?
> 2) What is the complexity of maintaining region_preference at the tenant level vs. per-storage-bucket?
> 3) What retention of audit logs do we offer by default and what needs to be added for contract-level guarantees?
>
> I've attached mockups and a toy API spec for discussion.
>
> Priya
> Product — Redwood Inference
> attachments: mockups-retention-ui.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention + deletion SLA requirements for Acme pilot

Priya — thanks for the clear spec. Quick technical notes from infra/serving:

- Enforcement model: There are two enforcement points: storage (object lifecycle + bucket policies) and serving (KV cache + index). Storage deletion is straightforward; ensuring immediate block from serving requires invalidation of keys in the runtime's KV cache and ensuring any persistent replicas are also cleared. That path is feasible but needs a coordinated rollback/fallback plan for in-flight requests.
- Region pinning: Per-tenant region_preference can be implemented as a metadata attribute that maps a tenant to a storage cluster/zone. The heavy lift is the scheduler and placement policy for existing objects (re-replication to US-only) — copying and re-sharding data at scale is non-trivial and will require a background migration job. For the pilot we recommend binding the tenant to a new US-only bucket and routing reads/writes there (no live re-replication).
- Deletion SLA: A contractual 30-day SLA for deletion completion is achievable if we control storage and the ops path, but cannot be guaranteed if copies exist in third-party backups or cloud provider replication outside our control. We should enumerate those exceptions in the contract.
- Auditability: We'll need to extend our audit stream to include signed deletion receipts (operation id, timestamp, actor, confirmation hash). This is a small extension to the existing audit pipeline but requires storage for those receipts for the contract duration.

Estimate for MVP (engineering effort, rough):
- Policy layer and API: 4–6 engineer-weeks (core infra + product API).
- Console: 1–2 sprints (design + frontend).
- Audit receipts: 1–2 engineer-weeks + storage cost.
- Region-binding ops flow (pilot): 3 engineer-days + runbook.

Short-term pilot recommendation: create US-only storage, bind Acme tenant, configure lifecycle rule for 30 days, and produce manual deletion receipts for the first 60 days while we ship the policy layer.

— Karthik

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention + deletion SLA requirements for Acme pilot

Thanks all — compliance notes:

- Deletion proof: signed deletion receipts are acceptable, but legal will expect chain-of-custody for any copies. We must document exactly what we can guarantee (primary + platform-managed replicas) and call out cloud provider-managed backups or long-term snapshots as exceptions.
- Exemption tags: any dataset-level exemption must require a signed request and will be logged as an administrative override. We should add an approval workflow in the console and a required justification field.
- Retention of audit logs: propose default 1 year, contractually adjustable. For Acme's 30-day deletion SLA we need deletion receipts retained for at least 2 years per their legal ask.

I'll work with security engineering to draft the language we can include in a SOC/compliance addendum for pilots.

Mina
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summary and action items:

1) Pilot path (short-term, 1–2 months):
   - Ops to provision US-only storage and bind Acme tenant (Rishi ops runbook).
   - Configure lifecycle rule to delete objects after 30 days.
   - Provide manual deletion receipts for the pilot window and weekly exports of audit logs.
2) Product MVP (10 weeks target):
   - Tenant retention policy API + Console (Priya: own spec).
   - Audit receipt extension (Karthik: infra work).
   - Administrative exemption workflow + approval (Mina: compliance requirements).
3) Legal/contract items:
   - Draft exceptions list (cloud provider backups, third-party copies) and SLA language (Mina will draft).

I'll set up a 30-minute sync this week to align timelines and confirm ops tasks. Priya, Karthik, Mina — can you each share a one-page scope/estimate by EOD Wednesday so I can respond to Acme and lock the pilot start?

Rishi
